chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform acts of kindness to everyone; if he is deserving of it, [then good for him], and if not, then you are deserving of it.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفَ: Acts of kindness or good deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of doing good to people who may not deserve it?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the universality of *al-ma'ruf* (goodness/kindness), decoupling the validity of the act from the worthiness of the recipient. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle that the virtue of the deed resides in the intention and action of the doer, ensuring spiritual reward regardless of whether the recipient reciprocates or deserves it. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining social harmony and personal piety in interactions with both the righteous and the ungrateful.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Perform the acts of kindness to everyone. So if he was deserving of it (fine), or else so you are its deserving one’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Provide Benevolent Assistance to everyone; if the recipient is not deserving, you are a deserving provider.” (This and Hadith 6 above are considered to apply when the provider has no knowledge of the condition of the recipient. Thus, what will come later does not contradict.)
